data.title: Initiation
data.notes:
The 4th album, by Todd Rundgren.

It is a one of the longest running single disc LPs ever issued (1 hour, 7 minutes and 34 seconds; side B's total time is almost 35½ minutes).

However, because of its fragility and reduced dynamic range, the following note was printed on the inner sleeve:
"Technical Note: Due to the amount of music on this disc (over one hour), two points must be emphasized. Firstly, if your needle is worn or damaged, it will ruin this disc immediately. Secondly, if the sound does not seem loud enough on your system, try re-recording the music onto tape. By the way, thanks for buying the album"

The final suite 'A Treatise On Cosmic Fire' was sped up by half a step to fit the disc with ease, this is why 'Prana' on the 'Real Man' 45RPM 7'' single sounds slower, as that was the speed that was intended to be heard, except all discs and CD reissues play the sped up version used for the original LP. To slow it to the correct speed, using software such as Audacity, reduce the speed by 5.94 percent (one half step).

data.title: Aja
data.notes:
Note: 1st USA vinyl pressings were issued with a release # AB-1006 on labels (likely a typo) and have AA-1006 printed on the rear cover/spine vs the corrected/amended AA-1006 releases reissued during the same year using AA for both labels & the cover.  

Aja (pronounced like "Asia") is the sixth studio album by Steely Dan. Released in 1977, the album peaked at number 3 on the US charts and at number 5 in the UK.  It was the band's first platinum album and became their best-selling studio release, eventually selling over five million copies. The album includes the hit songs Deacon Blues, as well as Peg and Josie. In 2010 the Library of Congress selected Aja for inclusion in the United States National Recording Registry based on its cultural, artistic or historical significance.

AJA is not considered "Soft Rock" nor is it "Yacht Rock"
